provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: In the original task, each shape is a group of diagonally connected cells (8-connectivity) that are not background. Every shape slides right by its own bounding-box width, so it lands right beside where it was. The factory works out where the original +x direction ends up in the visible grid. If the D4 index is 4 or more, rows are mirrored first, which turns +x into -x. Each clockwise turn then maps a direction (dy, dx) to (dx, -dy). The emitted program sets the background to the constant palette[0]. It finds 8-connected non-background components and erases all of them first. It then re-stamps each one, shifted along the visible direction by its own extent on that axis: height for vertical motion, width for horizontal. Cells keep their original colours. Grids may be rectangular, and anything pushed outside the grid is clipped, matching the archived solver.
draft_notes.limitations: The program assumes separate shapes never touch, even diagonally. The generator's row-separation constraint makes this true. Clipping at the grid edge copies the archived solver; the generator never actually produces out-of-bounds shifts. Demonstrations are not used, because the direction and background come from d4 and palette. The fixtures are consistent with the uniform rule.
